title: Cloud platform selection
transcript:
Platform Engineering Lead: Alright team, let's discuss our cloud infrastructure migration options. We've been looking at Google Cloud Platform, Microsoft Azure, and IBM Cloud.

SRE: I've got to say, managing Azure services internally seems like a challenge given our current expertise.

Finance Partner: And the costs for Google Cloud are steep in the long run compared to AWS.

Platform Engineering Lead: Agreed, and IBM Cloud also doesn't seem to fit well with our existing microservice architecture. So, it looks like we're leaning towards AWS.

CTO: But let's not make a hasty decision. We need to consider the initial setup cost and the migration timeline.

SRE: True, migrating to AWS will require a one-time investment of around $500,000.

Platform Engineering Lead: And the migration process needs to be completed within the next 6 months to avoid penalties from our current provider.

Finance Partner: (sighs) I understand the benefits, but I still can't stomach the upfront cost.

Platform Engineering Lead: I hear your concerns, but consider this: AWS offers the best balance of price, feature fit, and support quality. Our team can ramp up quickly on AWS services, minimizing onboarding time.

SRE: And once we're set up, the ongoing costs are lower compared to other options.

Finance Partner: I suppose I can't deny that, but let's keep an eye on our budget and explore potential cost-saving measures during the migration.

Platform Engineering Lead: Absolutely. Now, who do we want to assign ownership of this project to?

CTO: I'll take it upon myself to sign off, but I think the SRE team should own it.

Platform Engineering Lead: Sounds like a plan. Alright, let's commit to AWS for our cloud infrastructure. We've weighed the pros and cons and it seems like the best choice for us.

Finance Partner: (nods) I suppose it's the least expensive option in the long run. But let's keep an eye on the costs and find ways to mitigate the upfront expense.

(Off-topic exchange, light-hearted)

Platform Engineering Lead: So, any plans for the weekend, CTO?

CTO: Nothing much, just catching up on some sci-fi series. Care to join me for a watch party?

Platform Engineering Lead: I might be busy with the AWS migration plans, but I'll see what I can do. Let's catch up soon!

(End of off-topic exchange)

Platform Engineering Lead: Alright, let's get back to it. We have a lot to do before the migration process begins. SRE, shall we start drafting the project plan?

SRE: You got it. Let's get started!

CTO: Excellent! I'll sign off on the decision and we can get the ball rolling. Let's make this migration a success!

Title: Cloud Infrastructure Decision Summary

Decision: The organization remains committed to AWS for cloud infrastructure due to its superior balance of price, feature fit, and support quality. Migration from the current provider, IBM Cloud, has been hindered by insufficient compatibility with our existing microservice architecture.

Additionally, the SRE team will be instrumental in the migration process. Discussions with the finance partner led to the objection of the upfront cost associated with migrating to AWS, but the long-term costs of Google Cloud Platform were deemed higher.

An expedited migration timeline has been set to complete the process within the next six months to avoid penalties from our expiring contract with the current provider. Specifics regarding internal expertise and one-time costs associated with the migration will not be included in this record.
